title: Bounded-index reader soundness
statement: For every natural number $n$, bit string $x$, index $i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and bit string $r$, if the range-checked unary index reader of bound $n$ succeeds on $x$ with result $(i,r)$, then $x$ consists of $i$ ones followed by a zero, and then $r$.
hypotheses_covered: the range-checked unary index reader of bound $n$ succeeds on $x$ with result $(i,r)$
replaced:
If the range-checked unary reader with bound $n$ succeeds on a bit string $x$,
returning an index $i < n$ and a suffix $r$, then $x$ is exactly the
self-delimiting unary code of $i$ ($i$ ones and a closing zero) followed by
$r$.
